events.title: Death of Richard the Lionheart
events.description: King Richard I of England died from an infection after an arrow wound to his shoulder, which he received during a siege in France. His younger brother John succeeded him on the throne.
events.significance: Richard's death brought John to the throne. John's reign led to the sealing of Magna Carta in 1215, a landmark in the history of constitutional government.

events.title: The Church of Christ is organized
events.description: Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer and others formally organized the Church of Christ in New York. It was the beginning of the Latter Day Saint movement.
events.significance: The movement grew into a major American religious tradition. Its largest branch, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, now has millions of members around the world.

events.title: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens
events.description: After a gap of about 1,500 years, the Olympic Games returned in Athens, with athletes from several nations competing in the revived event.
events.significance: The Games became the world's leading international sporting event, and they are held every few years in different host cities.

events.title: The United States declares war on Germany
events.description: The U.S. Congress formally declared war on Germany, which brought America into World War I after years of neutrality.
events.significance: American money, supplies and soldiers helped tip the balance toward the Allies. The war also marked the country's emergence as a major world power.

events.title: Presidential plane shot down over Kigali
events.description: A plane carrying Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundian President Cyprien Ntaryamira was shot down as it approached Kigali, and both men were killed.
events.significance: The attack set off the Rwandan genocide, in which hundreds of thousands of people were killed over roughly 100 days.
